analysis.title: Global Reflections (Louis Miller, FICC & Equities, 13 Nov 2026)
key_insights: The post-midterm relief rally lasted under 24 hours and AI/geopolitics fatigue resumed. The desk favors a barbell of selective AI trades and defensive, immediate FCF/income generators.
The Power theme (GSENEPOW) is up post-midterms, IPPs (GSXUIPPS) are +15% off their lows, and Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) still offer defensive AI exposure.

Last week's technical washout set up an AI rebound, but appetite to digest NVDA-specific issues was short lived. Investors describe the earlier-week price action as a potential thematic bear market rally.

Whether the sell-off is a buy-the-dip or the start of a regime shift in equity leadership depends on whether an earnings bubble exists. Some pockets are 'over earning' and the search for where medium-term earnings growth settles has been painful.

Valuations in certain pockets already price excessive downward revisions to 2027 earnings. Renewed AI confidence could drive a doubling of memory stocks. The desk also likes adding longs on SPXXAI to balance AI exposure.

The market's biggest index weights lack free cash flow and non-cash earnings are a bigger share of earnings growth, so FCF is scarce and matters more. The desk expects high FCF generators to keep being rewarded in a higher-for-longer rates environment.
Preferred expression is long the US High vs Low FCF pair (GSPUFCFP), where recent outperformance came equally from the long and short legs. Quality's strength has come mostly from the short leg.
The European High vs Low FCF pair (GSPEFCFP) lagged the US version over the summer but has started to catch up aggressively, and the desk expects that to continue in coming weeks.
Short theme: the Lending Sensitive basket (GSXULEND), businesses with capital needs that may be crowded out by other capital market needs.

China high-dividend trade is working: stable cash generation, yields and mostly domestic earnings buffered volatility, and National Team buying supports SOE/high-dividend names. Listed Chinese companies returned more than Rmb2tn a year via dividends and buybacks in each of the past three years.

The China High Dividend basket (GSXACHHN) is up 8pp over 3m while CSI 300 is down 15pp. Asia colleagues favor Value, Dividend and Cash Return over longer-duration growth given wide US-China yield differentials.

Europe has one of the lowest betas to AI (SXXP 2y daily beta to GSPUARTI below 0.05). The desk expects investors to return to Europe for AI diversification, though the full bull case still hinges on a US-Iran resolution.
The EU High and Stable Margins basket (GSXEMARG) combines low AI correlation with a defensive skew and has just started to break out versus the market.

French Domestics (GSXEFRDO) rallied 10% from October lows, which the desk sees as premature. Credit conditions are difficult, political uncertainty is high, and S&P's credit rating review on Nov 27 is the near-term catalyst.

Momentum is in a regime shift: correlation between 12m momentum (GSPRHIMO) and 3m momentum (GSPRHMO3) is now negative, and AI names in the short leg of 3m and 6m momentum (GSPRHMO6) have risen sharply. Infotech was net sold in 3m and 6m momentum but slightly bought in 12m.
Momentum 60-day volatility is 3.5x that of SPX, so the desk expects more rotations and reversals until the market settles on new long-term leadership.
